title: Stick and Stone
author: Beth Ferry

demand_candidate.rationale: Short friendship and anti-bullying story with concrete object characters, simple emotions, and strong classroom-community bundle potential.

hero.name: Stick and Stone
hero.description: A thin stick character and a round stone character, each drawn with simple stick-figure-style faces and limbs (pencil and watercolor illustrations by Tom Lichtenheld); they are the title duo shown together on the cover.

book_summary: Stick and Stone are each lonely until Stick stands up for Stone when a bullying Pinecone teases him at the playground, and the two become inseparable best friends. They explore, play, and blow bubbles together until a storm blows Stick out to sea; Stone searches everywhere and finally rescues Stick, who is stuck upside down in a puddle, proving the pair make 'a perfect 10' together.

fringe_justifications.Stone: Stone is the second title character, round and lonely at first, who later searches for and rescues Stick — a co-lead of the entire story.
fringe_justifications.Pinecone: Pinecone is the prickly antagonist who mocks Stone at the playground until Stick stands up to him, driving the story's central conflict.
fringe_justifications.storm: A windstorm/hurricane blows through partway in the book and carries Stick away, separating the two friends and starting the second half of the plot.
fringe_justifications.puddle: Stone finally finds Stick stuck upside down in a puddle after searching everywhere, the key discovery scene near the book's end.
fringe_justifications.swing: Pinecone teases Stone specifically because he cannot balance on the playground swing, the scene that sparks Stick's defense of Stone.
fringe_justifications.splash: Stone rescues Stick by leaping into the puddle with a big splash that dislodges him, the climactic rescue action.
fringe_justifications.friend: Becoming friends is the book's central theme, marked by the line describing Stick standing up for Stone as 'what sticks (stick up for people) do.'
fringe_justifications.alone: The book opens with both Stick and Stone feeling very alone before they meet, the emotional starting point of the story.
fringe_justifications.rescue: Stone must search for and rescue Stick after the storm carries him away, the main event of the story's second half.
fringe_justifications.ocean: The hurricane carries Stick out to sea near the ocean/seashore where the pair earlier watched dolphins together.
fringe_justifications.sorry: At the end, Pinecone apologizes to Stone, saying he is sorry for teasing him, resolving the bullying subplot.

grounding_note: Confirmed via multiple sources (Kirkus, BookPage, Goodreads, Books4Learning, publisher/retailer copy) that this is the 2015 Beth Ferry / Tom Lichtenheld picture book in which Stick defends Stone from bullying Pinecone, the two become friends, a storm separates them, and Stone rescues Stick from a puddle. Plot details are consistent across all sources, so confidence is high.
